# La–Fe–Si τ1/τ2 refit — decision rules, FROZEN 19 Nov 2026 (consolidates Addenda A–C of `FROZEN_SPEC.md`; format as the Cr–Fe–Ni Pilot-M pre-registration)

**Status: FROZEN 19 Nov 2026**, sha256 of this note and of the scripts in `PreReg_Refit.sha256`, committed **before** any residual, fitted parameter or held-out loss of the Addendum-B model was computed.

**Disclosure — what had been seen before this freeze (so it can be checked):**
1. Refit 1 (12 parameters, weak regulariser) and refit 2 (6 constants, regulariser 1000) on the 17/7 split: **both rejected** (RESULTS.md, merged PRs #17, #18). These motivated Addendum B.
2. Equilibrium counts of the Addendum-B data (30 train / 17 held-out / 24 excluded) — counts only.
3. Residuals of the **Feng-reconstructed baseline only** on its 24 evaluable equilibria: phase set matches 6/24, within scatter 2/24; no systematic τ1/τ2 Si shift (mean ΔSi −0.5 / −0.25 at.%).
4. **Intermediate training-loss lines** of the Addendum-B runs (at epoch 360: fit 9.7e3, frozen prior baseline 2.5e4) — seen while writing this note. No fitted parameter value, no held-out loss, no residual of the Addendum-B models.
5. **Design consequence of item 4, decided now:** the prior baseline (new phases at an arbitrary −30 kJ/mol-atom) is a weak comparator — any fit of the new phases beats it. A **control run** (new-phase parameters fitted, τ1/τ2 frozen at the published values, otherwise identical) is therefore added (§4.4); the τ1/τ2 verdict is taken against it, not against the prior.

## 1. Question and nature
Do the Niitsu & Kainuma 2012 equilibria contain information that moves the τ1/τ2 parameters of the sign-corrected Feng reconstruction away from the published values, in a way that improves held-out description? Methods/negative-result study; **not** a re-assessment; fitted energies of LaFe2Si2, LaFeSi, LaFeSi2 are effective values, never to be used as thermodynamic data without validation.

## 2. Observables (fixed)
- **L_train, L_held:** eqopt loss on the 30 training (1173, 1273–1523, 1573 K) and 17 held-out (1373 K) equilibria; data part only (stable + unstable terms; regulariser reported separately), same settings and μ′ relaxation for all models.
- **Residuals:** Addendum C — equilibrium at the nominal composition and T; phase-set match; ΔSi, ΔLa of BCC_A2/FCC_A1/LIQUID/TAU1/TAU2 in at.%; **within scatter** = phase set matches and all |ΔSi| ≤ 2.0, |ΔLa| ≤ 1.0 at.%. Reported separately for the 30 training and 17 held-out points and per equilibrium (which reproduced, which outliers, kind of outlier: phase set / composition).
- **Systematic shift:** mean signed ΔSi of TAU1 and TAU2 overall and per temperature; systematic if |mean| > 1.0 at.% and ≥ 75 % same sign.
- **Gate quantities:** A3 (τ1 fraction at La(Fe11.5Si1.5), 1373 K ≥ 0.9), A5 (τ1-dominant window along La(Fe1−xSix)13 overlaps 0.096–0.229), D > 0 at the 15 descriptor points, fitted formation energy of each new phase at 1373 K in [−80, 0] kJ/mol-atom.

## 3. Models (fixed)
- **M0 Feng baseline** (original TDB; 24 evaluable equilibria; residuals only).
- **M1 prior:** M0 + three stoichiometric compounds at the frozen −30 kJ/mol-atom prior, all parameters frozen (lr 1e-9).
- **M2 control:** M1 with the 6 new-phase parameters (w, v per phase) fitted, τ1/τ2 frozen. Regulariser 100, lr 0.1, 1000 epochs, seed 42, latent_mu_lr 100.
- **M3 full:** M2 plus the 6 τ1/τ2 constants free (12 parameters), same settings.

## 4. Procedure and gates (fixed; applied in this order, once)
1. **Run validity (not a gate):** M1, M2, M3 train to epoch 1000; held-out evaluations at 400 epochs with lr 1e-9; residual files have one row per model × evaluable equilibrium. Script/environment faults → fix or pin, qualify and repeat the whole run; failures caused by the data or the model stay failures.
2. **Fit quality (M3 vs M1):** C1 L_train(M3) ≤ 0.90·L_train(M1); C2 L_held(M3) ≤ 1.05·L_held(M1); C3, C4 as Addendum B (gate quantities and |w| ≤ 20, |v| ≤ 1).
3. **Beyond the prior — does τ1/τ2 refitting add anything? (M3 vs M2):**
   - **T1** L_held(M3) ≤ 0.95·L_held(M2);
   - **T2** within-scatter count of M3 on the 17 held-out points ≥ that of M2 (not lower) **and** on all 47 points ≥ that of M2 + 2;
   - **T3** the six fitted τ constants are not all within the solver noise (|Δ| > 50 J/mol for at least two).
4. **Verdict (single rule):**
   - **"τ1/τ2 refit justified"** only if C1–C4 and T1–T3 all hold. Further refit effort is then justified, with the caveat that the competing-phase energies are effective.
   - **otherwise "Niitsu data insufficient to move the model"**: the sign-corrected Feng reconstruction is frozen as "best available given the public data"; no rescue, no further sweeps in this thread.
   - Whatever the verdict, the three requested diagnostics (training reproduction, held-out residuals, systematic shift vs the Feng description) are reported; they cannot change the verdict.
5. **Recording:** every fitted parameter (w, v of each new phase; τ1/τ2 w; the absolute parameter strings in the optimised TDB), the optimised TDBs, train/held-out inputs, logs' final-epoch lines and the per-equilibrium residual tables are committed (as `.txt`/`.tsv` and `.tdb`; the repository ignores `.csv`). Ledger entry either way.

## 5. Prior expectation (written before any computation of the Addendum-B models)
Refits 1 and 2 moved nothing useful; Feng's assessment saw the same data. I expect "Niitsu data insufficient to move the model", with M3 ≈ M2; a chance that the added phases reduce phase-set outliers (the dominant failure of M0) without changing τ1/τ2.

## 6. Scripts and environment (hashed at the freeze)
`make_inputs.py` (options `--constants-only --ternary --no-tau`), `make_valid_tdbs.py`, `evaluate.py`, `residuals.py`, `config_tern.yaml`, `config_tern_base.yaml`, `FROZEN_SPEC.md`; eqopt commit 2b1d4b4 unmodified, torch 2.15.0, pycalphad as installed; seed 42. Data: Niitsu 2012 tielines (own transcription, recovered from git `1b83f71^`).

## 7. Limits
17+30 equilibria of one study at 1173–1573 K; tie-lines give relative energies only; nominal-composition equilibria are sensitive to mass-balance-flagged rows; ternary phases modelled as stoichiometric (no Fe/Si solubility); LaSi2 variants and the AlB2-type phase still excluded (24 equilibria); one regulariser value, no sweep; the scatter band (2.0/1.0 at.%) is a stated judgement.
-e

# FILE: stage_four/calphad_lafesi/refit_tau12/residuals.py
---
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Per-equilibrium residuals (FROZEN_SPEC.md Addendum C).
Usage: python residuals.py TIELINES.csv OUT.csv LABEL=TDB [LABEL=TDB ...]"""
import sys, csv, warnings, numpy as np
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
from pycalphad import Database, equilibrium, variables as v
from make_inputs import MAP, TER_MAP
ALL = dict(MAP, **TER_MAP)
SOL = {'BCC_A2', 'FCC_A1', 'LIQUID', 'TAU1', 'TAU2'}
COMPS = ['LA', 'FE', 'SI', 'VA']
def calc(db, la, si, T):
    r = equilibrium(db, COMPS, list(db.phases), {v.X('LA'): la, v.X('SI'): si, v.T: T, v.P: 101325, v.N: 1},
                    calc_opts={'pdens': 2000})
    P = np.array(r.Phase).ravel(); N = np.array(r.NP).ravel()
    XL = np.array(r.X.sel(component='LA')).ravel(); XS = np.array(r.X.sel(component='SI')).ravel()
    out = {}
    for p, n, a, b in zip(P, N, XL, XS):
        if str(p) in ('', 'nan') or np.isnan(n) or n <= 1e-3: continue
        out.setdefault(str(p), (float(n), float(a), float(b)))
    return out
def main(ties, out, models):
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(ties, encoding='utf-8')))
    dbs = {k: Database(p) for k, p in models}
    res = []
    for i, r in enumerate(rows):
        if any(r[f'phase{j}'] and (r[f'La{j}'] == '' or r[f'Si{j}'] == '') for j in (1, 2, 3)): continue  # n.d. rows
        ph = [(r[f'phase{j}'], float(r[f'La{j}']) / 100, float(r[f'Si{j}']) / 100) for j in (1, 2, 3) if r[f'phase{j}']]
        if any(p not in ALL for p, _, _ in ph): continue
        exp = {ALL[p]: (la, si) for p, la, si in ph}
        for k, db in dbs.items():
            if any(n not in db.phases for n in exp): continue   # model cannot evaluate this equilibrium
            try: c = calc(db, float(r['nominal_La']) / 100, float(r['nominal_Si']) / 100, float(r['T_K']))
            except Exception as e: res.append([k, i, r['T_K'], '', 'ERR', str(e)[:40]]); continue
            match = set(c) == set(exp)
            dS = [(n, 100 * (c[n][2] - exp[n][1]), 100 * (c[n][1] - exp[n][0])) for n in exp if n in SOL and n in c]
            ok = match and all(abs(a) <= 2.0 and abs(b) <= 1.0 for _, a, b in dS)
            res.append([k, i, r['T_K'], '+'.join(sorted(exp)), '+'.join(sorted(c)), int(match), int(ok),
                        ';'.join(f'{n}:{a:+.1f}/{b:+.1f}' for n, a, b in dS)])
    with open(out, 'w', newline='') as f:
        w = csv.writer(f); w.writerow(['model', 'row', 'T_K', 'exp_phases', 'calc_phases', 'set_match', 'within_scatter', 'dSi/dLa_at%'])
        w.writerows(res)
    for k in dbs:
        m = [x for x in res if x[0] == k and x[4] != 'ERR']
        print(f'{k}: n={len(m)} set-match {sum(x[5] for x in m)} within-scatter {sum(x[6] for x in m)}')
    for k in dbs:
        for tau in ('TAU1', 'TAU2'):
            d = [float(s.split(':')[1].split('/')[0]) for x in res if x[0] == k and len(x) > 7 for s in x[7].split(';') if s.startswith(tau)]
            if d:
                print(f'  {k} {tau}: n={len(d)} mean dSi {np.mean(d):+.2f} frac_same_sign {max(np.mean(np.array(d) > 0), np.mean(np.array(d) < 0)):.2f}')
if __name__ == '__main__':
    main(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], [a.split('=', 1) for a in sys.argv[3:]])
-e

# FILE: stage_four/calphad_lafesi/refit_tau12/RESULTS.md
---
# τ1/τ2 refit — results (19 Nov 2026)

Spec: `FROZEN_SPEC.md` (frozen before the run). Tool: authors' `eqopt` 2b1d4b4, unmodified.
Data: 17 training equilibria (1173, 1273–1523, 1573 K), 7 held out (1373 K); 47 of 71
Niitsu equilibria unusable because they contain phases absent from the TDB.

## Outcome: **refit REJECTED — baseline retained**

| criterion | result | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| C1 train loss ≤ 90 % of baseline | 9.20e3 vs 1.02e4 (frozen-parameter, μ′-relaxed) = **90.2 %** | fail (marginal) |
| C2 held-out 1373 K loss ≤ 105 % of baseline | 8.81e3 vs 1.05e3 = **840 %** (unstable-phase term 178 → 6870) | **fail, large** |
| C3 A3/A5 still hold | A3 literally yes, but τ1 falls from single-phase to 21 % of the assemblage (63 % FCC, 16 % LaSi2_X); A5 window 0.08–0.24 → 0.14–0.26 (still overlaps 0.096–0.229) | pass on the letter, substantive degradation |
| C4 corrections sane | max |Δconst| 0.26 kJ/mol, max |ΔT coeff| 2.6 J/mol/K | pass |

Note on the baseline: the raw first-epoch loss (1.37e5) is not a fair baseline, since μ′ is still
unrelaxed; the comparison uses a run with the model learning rate 1e-9 (parameters frozen) and the
same latent-μ settings.

## Fitted corrections (J/mol, J/mol/K)
| parameter | Δconst | ΔT coeff |
|---|---|---|
| τ1 G(La:Fe) | +173.9 | +2.620 |
| τ1 G(La:Si) | −170.0 | −1.238 |
| τ1 L(La:Fe,Si) | −150.6 | −0.956 |
| τ2 G(La:Fe) | −6.2 | +2.074 |
| τ2 G(La:Si) | −261.6 | +0.081 |
| τ2 L(La:Fe,Si) | −159.1 | +0.873 |

## Descriptor (reported)
D = G(competing, τ suspended) − G(all), J/mol-atom, at x = 1.2–2.0, 1050–1200 °C:
baseline 1300–3170, refit 0–635. The refit removes most of τ1's stabilisation at the
magnetocaloric composition. GM at La(Fe11.5Si1.5), 1373 K: −91444 → −89417 J/mol-atom (+2.0 kJ).

## Interpretation and limits
- The training set is tiny and one-sided: 1373 K, where τ1 is best constrained, is the held-out set,
  and the equilibria with LaFe2Si2/LaFeSi/LaFeSi2 are all missing, so nothing in the loss
  penalises τ1 for losing to FCC + LaSi2. The fit reduces the loss mainly by lowering the
  unstable-phase penalty at other temperatures at the expense of the τ1 window.
- Only phase equilibria enter the loss (no DSC, no EPMA). Feng EPMA check not run.
- Not tested: more training data (adding 1373 K, with a different held-out split such as
  leave-one-table-out), phases added to the TDB so more equilibria become usable, a stronger
  regulariser (`regularize_difference`) or fewer free parameters (e.g. only the 6 constants).
  Not tuned here, to keep the frozen spec honest.
- Inputs recovered from git history (the CSVs are gitignored). Run artefacts (logs, optimized TDB)
  are not committed; reproduce with `make_inputs.py`, `eqopt-calphad … --config config.yaml`,
  `make_valid_tdbs.py`, `evaluate.py`.

Setup frozen in `FROZEN_SPEC.md` Addendum A before the run (6 constants, one regulariser value, no sweep).

| criterion | result | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| C1 train loss ≤ 90 % of baseline | data loss (stable + unstable) 1.002e4 vs 1.020e4 = **98 %** (total 1.01e4 incl. regulariser 41.5) | fail |
| C2 held-out 1373 K loss ≤ 105 % of baseline | 1.13e3 vs 1.05e3 = **107.6 %** (stable 871 → 917, unstable 178 → 209) | fail (marginal) |

Fitted constants (J/mol): τ1 G(La:Fe) −3.6, G(La:Si) −47.0, L −29.4; τ2 G(La:Fe) +173.3, G(La:Si) +75.0, L +52.5.

## Reading
Strong regularisation does what it should for safety — τ1 is no longer destroyed (the first refit's failure) —
but the 17 training equilibria with 6 constants then offer only a ~2 % loss reduction, and the held-out
loss rises slightly. Together with the first refit this says the usable Niitsu data do not constrain the
τ1/τ2 parameters beyond the published ones: the loss is dominated by terms (unstable-phase penalties
from LaSi2/La–Si compounds, stable-phase offsets of the Fe–Si phases) that τ1/τ2 constants cannot move.
Not tried: adding the missing ternary phases (LaFe2Si2, LaFeSi, LaFeSi2) so the 47 excluded
equilibria become usable — the data most informative for τ1/τ2 competition — or a different split.

# Addendum B/C results — fitted ternary compounds, residual analysis (19 Nov 2026)

Rules: `PreReg_Refit_FROZEN_20261119.md` (hashes `PreReg_Refit.sha256`, commit cbd7fc4, before any Addendum-B result).
Models: M1 prior (new phases at −30 kJ/mol-atom, frozen) · M2 control (new-phase parameters fitted, τ1/τ2 published) · M3 full (new phases + 6 τ constants fitted).
All values, TDBs, inputs and residual tables: `results_addB/` (`all_parameters.tsv`, `new_phase_parameters.tsv`, `tau_constants.tsv`, `final_epoch_losses.tsv`, `residuals_*.tsv`, `*_optimized.tdb`).
Helper `make_valid_b.py` was added after the freeze (dummy symbol for held-out evaluation; no rule change).

## Verdict: **"Niitsu data insufficient to move the model"** — the Feng reconstruction stays frozen as best available.

| rule | quantity | result | |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | L_train(M3) ≤ 0.90·L_train(M1) (data part) | 7.79e3 vs 2.45e4 = 32 % | pass |
| C2 | L_held(M3) ≤ 1.05·L_held(M1) | 2.45e3 vs 3.03e4 = 8 % | pass |
| C3 | A3 (τ1 fraction ≥ 0.9), A5 overlap, D > 0 | τ1 = 1.00; window 0.10–0.26 (M2: 0.08–0.24); D 99–2385 J/mol-atom, all > 0 | pass |
| C4 | \|w\| ≤ 20, \|v\| ≤ 1; ΔG_f(1373 K) ∈ [−80, 0] | ΔG_f −57 … −67 kJ/mol-atom ok, but **\|v\| = 1.96–2.65 for all three new phases** | **fail** |
| T1 | L_held(M3) ≤ 0.95·L_held(M2) | 2.45e3 vs 2.35e3 = 104 % | **fail** |
| T2 | within scatter: M3 ≥ M2 on held-out and ≥ M2 + 2 on all 47 | held-out 1 vs 2; all 47: 3 vs 4 | **fail** |
| T3 | ≥ 2 τ constants move > 50 J/mol | 5 of 6 do (see below) | pass |

Verdict rule: "justified" needs C1–C4 and T1–T3 all → not met (C4, T1, T2 fail).

## The three requested diagnostics
1. **Training points (30):** loss falls 2.45e4 → 7.8e3 (M1 → M3) but only M3: 2 of 30 reproduced within scatter (set match 4 of 30); M2: 2 (6); M1: 1 (4).
2. **Held-out points (17, 1373 K):** within scatter M1 1, M2 2, M3 1; phase set matches 2 / 4 / 2. M3 ≈ M2 in loss (104 %), slightly worse in residuals. On all 47: 2 / 4 / 3. (Feng baseline M0 on its 24 evaluable points: 2.)
3. **Systematic shifts:** by the frozen rule none: M3 τ1 mean ΔSi +1.48 at.% (69 % same sign, below the 75 % threshold); τ2 +0.30. Descriptive (not a rule): in M0–M2 the calculated τ1 Si content runs from **+4.9 at.% (1173 K) to −2.1 at.% (1573 K)** relative to experiment — the temperature dependence of the τ1 boundary is too weak in the model; **M3 leaves it unchanged** (+4.87 at 1173 K, −1.68 at 1573 K). The dominant failure everywhere is the phase set (≤ 10 of 47 sets match), not the τ1/τ2 compositions.

## Fitted values (all recorded in `results_addB/`)
New phases (M3 / M2): LaFe2Si2 G = ΣGHSER − 151710.8 − 122.63·T (M2: −151502.4 − 125.45·T); LaFeSi −91168.3 − 79.32·T (M2 −91141.8 − 79.65·T); LaFeSi2 −120666.7 − 78.20·T (both runs identical to 10 digits — observation: the optimum was the same irrespective of the τ constants; not interpreted). ΔG_f(1373 K) −64.0 / −66.7 / −57.0 kJ/mol-atom (M3). These are effective numbers, not thermodynamic data.
τ constants (M3, published → fitted, J/mol): τ1 La:Fe 2300 → 2675.8 (+376); τ1 La:Si 37000 → 36964.2 (−36); τ1 L −242114 → −242120.5 (−6); τ2 La:Fe 6500 → 7096.4 (+596); τ2 La:Si 22500 → 22682.2 (+182); τ2 L −241114 → −240968.5 (+146). T-coefficients not free (constants-only).

## Reading and limits
- τ1/τ2 refitting adds nothing measurable beyond fitting the competing phases alone (M3 vs M2: held-out loss +4 %, residuals no better). Adding the three phases is what removes most of the loss, but the new-phase T-slopes go beyond the frozen sanity bound, so those energies are not credible as data.
- The regulariser term is large (1.8e3 of 9.5e3), so the fit is regulariser-limited, not data-limited; one value (100), no sweep, by rule.
- 17 + 30 equilibria, tie-lines (relative energies), 1173–1573 K, nominal-composition equilibria sensitive to mass-balance-flagged rows, ternary phases stoichiometric, LaSi2 variants / AlB2 phase still excluded (24 equilibria). Thread closed under the frozen rule: reconstructed Feng τ1/τ2 stays.

# Addendum D results — τ1 temperature-dependence bias vs the WP4b descriptor (20 Nov 2026)

Plan frozen before the run (`FROZEN_SPEC.md` Addendum D, commit 14449c0). Model M0 = Feng-reconstructed baseline on the merged binaries (nothing fitted). Files: `results_addD/` (M0 TDB, `M0_ranges.tsv`, `M0_D.tsv`, `addD_analysis.txt`, calc log), scripts `tau1_window.py`, `addD_analysis.py`.

## Finding 1 — the calculated τ1 and τ2 windows do not move with temperature
Calculated τ1 single-phase range (y = Si/(Fe+Si) in La(Fe1−ySiy)13): **0.085–0.090 / 0.235–0.240 at every temperature from 1173 to 1573 K.**
Measured (Niitsu): 0.086–0.211 (1173 K), 0.096–0.229 (1373 K), 0.162–0.279 (1573 K), i.e. the window shifts to higher Si with temperature
(stated in Niitsu's abstract). Calc − exp, lower / upper boundary: 1173 K +0.004 / +0.024; 1373 K −0.011 / +0.006; 1573 K −0.077 / −0.039.
τ2: 0.27–0.43 → 0.275–0.42, measured 0.251–0.398, 0.266–0.402, 0.291–0.376. Two separate model errors:
**position** (the missing temperature shift: the bias runs from positive at low T to strongly negative at 1573 K) and **width** (calculated τ1 window 0.145–0.155 vs measured 0.117–0.133, 0.02–0.04 too wide, 0.038 at 1573 K).
Not Si-rich-boundary-only: the Table-7 τ1+τ2 tie-line residuals (+0.4 / −0.4 at.% in 1423/1473 K) describe the **Si-rich** end of τ1, where the calculation is good.

## Finding 2 — descriptor sensitivity: material inside the window (frozen rule)
The descriptor compositions (y = 0.092–0.154) sit near the **Si-poor** boundary, where the model–experiment offset is the large one.
The rule applies the per-temperature offset (not a uniform shift); the experimental boundary at 1323/1423/1473 K is linearly **interpolated** between the measured 1173/1373/1573 K ranges.
| T | exp Si-poor boundary (interp.) | calc | δy | est. ΔD (J/mol-atom) | ΔD/D over x = 1.2 … 2.0 | class |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1323 K (1050 °C) | 0.0935 | 0.085 | −0.0085 | −258 | 20, 14, 11, 9, 8 % | borderline (x ≤ 1.6), not material (x ≥ 1.8) |
| 1423 K (1150 °C) | 0.1125 | 0.085 | −0.0275 | −800 | 62, 44, 35, 30, 26 % | **material** at all x |
| 1473 K (1200 °C) | 0.1290 | 0.085 | −0.0440 | −1246 | 96, 69, 55, 47, 41 % | **material** at all x |
Sign: the model keeps τ1 stable at lower Si than measured, so the descriptor (stability margin of τ1 against its competitors) is **overestimated** at the Si-poor end at the high-temperature end of the window.

## Caveats (read with Finding 2)
- ΔD is a first-order estimate: a composition offset δy converted with the finite-difference slope of D along x (≈ 2.8–3.0 × 10⁴ J/mol-atom per unit y); not a recomputed descriptor.
- There is **no measurement of the lower boundary between 1373 K and 1573 K**; at 1423/1473 K the "experiment" is a linear interpolation, and the size of the bias at 1473 K rests on the single 1573 K range (0.162). The 1373 K datum alone gives δy = −0.011 (borderline/not material). A direct measurement or a Feng-assessment value at 1423–1473 K would settle it.
- The bias is that of **our reconstruction** (merged binaries FeLa-23Su/LaSi-10Zho/FeSi-17Cui); whether Feng's own TDB has the same flat window is not testable with the public data. The 20-binary-combination band of WP4 could be repeated for the window to see how much of it is binary choice.
- The M3 refit left the window unchanged; the refit does not address this bias.

## Limitation statement (the "material" shape of the pre-agreed three)
"The reconstruction does not reproduce the temperature shift of the τ1 single-phase region towards higher Si content (calculated Si-poor boundary 0.085–0.09 at all temperatures vs measured 0.086 → 0.096 → 0.162 at 1173/1373/1573 K), and its τ1 window is 0.02–0.04 too wide. Inside the descriptor window this is material for the stability margin D at 1150–1200 °C (estimated 26–96 % of D, using an interpolated experimental boundary) and borderline at 1050 °C; D at 1150–1200 °C is overestimated at the Si-poor end. D results from 1050 °C are the least affected."

---
# Addendum E results — is the flat τ1 window a binary-choice effect? (20 Nov 2026)

Plan and rules frozen before the run (`FROZEN_SPEC.md` Addendum E, commit ab33236); data and per-combination table in `results_addD/` (`ens_w*.tsv`, `ens_analysis.txt`); scripts `ensemble_window.py`, `ensemble_analysis.py`. All 20 combinations of the WP4 band computed (0 failures); the M0 consistency check passed.

## Result: **20 of 20 combinations are flat** → by the frozen rule, **the flat τ1 window is not a binary-choice effect** (it comes with the Feng τ parameters as reconstructed)
- Shift of the Si-poor boundary between 1173 and 1573 K: −0.005 (15 combinations) or 0.000 (5); measured +0.076. No combination reproduces the measured shift.
- Position and width do depend on the binaries, but only through the **La–Si** file: with LaSi-10Zho the τ1 Si-poor boundary is 0.085–0.090 (width 0.150 at 1373 K); with LaSi-20Xu 0.065–0.070 (width 0.165–0.170). The Fe–La choice changes it by at most 0.005; **the five Fe–Si files give identical windows** at the grid resolution (0.005). Measured at 1373 K: Si-poor boundary 0.096, width 0.133 — the binary choice moves the model *away* from the measured width in both cases (0.150–0.170).
- So the binary choice shifts the window by up to 0.02 in y (comparable to the −0.011 residual at 1373 K) but cannot produce the missing temperature shift (0.076 at 1573 K).
- Adding the three fitted ternary compounds (Addendum B, M2/M3) also left the window essentially unchanged (0.08–0.24 → 0.08–0.24, M3 0.10–0.26 at 1373 K, 0.02 grid), so the missing LaFe2Si2/LaFeSi/LaFeSi2 competitors are not the explanation either.

## What this does and does not establish
- It does **not** show that Feng's published TDB has the flat window: the shared cause is the τ1/τ2 and ternary parameters as transcribed from Table 5 (sign-corrected). The cause could be the published assessment, or a remaining transcription/reconstruction issue in those parameters. The public data cannot separate the two; only the authors' TDB (Data Availability: on request) can.
- τ3–τ6 are absent from the production TDB (unreconstructable, TAU36_RECONSTRUCTION.md); their possible role at the Si-poor boundary is untested.

## Limitation statement for the descriptor (final form)
"In our reconstruction of the Feng assessment (merged SGTE binaries; τ3–τ6 not reconstructable), the calculated τ1 single-phase region does not move with temperature (Si-poor boundary y = 0.085–0.09 at 1173–1573 K; measured 0.086, 0.096, 0.162) and is 0.02–0.04 too wide. All 20 binary combinations of the WP4 band give the same flat window (shift −0.005 to 0 against the measured +0.076); the binary choice only moves it by up to 0.02 through the La–Si file, so the flatness is not a binary-choice effect. Because the descriptor compositions lie near the Si-poor boundary, the stability margin D is overestimated there: by a first-order estimate, 26–62 % of D at 1150 °C and 41–96 % at 1200 °C (material) and 8–20 % at 1050 °C (borderline); at 1423/1473 K the experimental boundary is interpolated between measurements at 1373 and 1573 K and the size at 1473 K rests on the single 1573 K range. Whether the flat window belongs to the published assessment or to our reconstruction of it is not decidable from public data. D at 1050 °C is the least affected."

---
# Final limitation statement (20 Nov 2026) — supersedes the two earlier "limitation statement" paragraphs above

Corrections after review: (i) the descriptor bias is driven by the missing temperature dependence (flatness) of the Si-poor boundary, not by the window position; (ii) the ternary-phase check is an effective-phase, single-temperature, 0.02-grid check; (iii) the 20-combination run is a sensitivity check, not the ensemble method; (iv) "identical" for the Fe–Si files is at the 0.005 grid resolution. No new calculation; no frozen rule changed.

> The reconstructed τ1 window is flat in temperature and too wide. The descriptor bias at 1150–1200 °C comes from the missing temperature dependence of the Si-poor boundary, not from the window position: the measured boundary rises from 0.086 to 0.162 between 1173 and 1573 K, the calculated one stays at 0.085–0.09, and the gap grows with temperature (−0.0085 at 1323 K, −0.0275 at 1423 K, −0.044 at 1473 K; these three offsets use an experimental boundary interpolated between the measurements at 1173, 1373 and 1573 K). By a first-order estimate this is 8–20 % of D at 1050 °C, 26–62 % at 1150 °C and 41–96 % at 1200 °C (D overestimated at the Si-poor end). A 20-combination sensitivity check found the flat window in all 20 combinations, so within this check the flatness is not a binary-choice effect. The La–Si edge moves the window position by up to 0.02 but not its temperature dependence; the five Fe–Si files gave windows identical to the 0.005 grid resolution, and the Fe–La choice moves the window by at most 0.005. Adding fitted effective ternary phases (LaFe₂Si₂, LaFeSi, LaFeSi₂) did not change the window in this check (one temperature, 0.02 grid). The bias is that of our reconstruction; whether Feng's published TDB has the same flat window cannot be decided from public data, and the 1423/1473 K offsets rest on a single measurement (the 1573 K range). The 1050 °C results are least affected.

**Conditional on the interpolation (added 20 Nov 2026, no new calculation).** The "material" class at 1423–1473 K rests on the straight-line interpolation between the measured 1373 and 1573 K ranges; 1373 K is the only measured point inside the descriptor window (1323–1473 K, near its low end) and the 1573 K range (0.162) is the only measurement that pulls the boundary up. In the minimal-offset scenario in which the measured Si-poor boundary stays at its 1373 K value (0.096) up to 1473 K, the offset would be −0.011 (≈310–320 J/mol-atom, 10–25 % of D by the same first-order estimate), which the frozen rule classes as borderline, not material. The class is therefore *material if the interpolation is right, borderline if it is not*; the direction (D overestimated at the Si-poor end, growing with temperature) does not depend on it.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Addendum D: tau1/tau2 single-phase ranges along La(Fe1-ySiy)13 vs Niitsu, and WP4b descriptor sensitivity.
Usage: python tau1_window.py M0.tdb OUT_PREFIX"""
import sys, warnings, numpy as np
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
from pycalphad import Database, equilibrium, variables as v
db = Database(sys.argv[1]); out = sys.argv[2]
COMPS = ['LA', 'FE', 'SI', 'VA']; ALL = list(db.phases); COMP = [p for p in ALL if p not in ('TAU1', 'TAU2')]
def frac(phases, la, si, T, pd=800):
    r = equilibrium(db, COMPS, phases, {v.X('LA'): la, v.X('SI'): si, v.T: T, v.P: 101325, v.N: 1}, calc_opts={'pdens': pd})
    P = np.array(r.Phase).ravel(); N = np.array(r.NP).ravel(); f = {}
    for p, n in zip(P, N):
        if str(p) not in ('', 'nan') and not np.isnan(n) and n > 1e-4: f[str(p)] = f.get(str(p), 0) + float(n)
    return f, float(np.array(r.GM).ravel()[0])
TS = [1173, 1273, 1323, 1373, 1423, 1473, 1523, 1573]; YS = np.arange(0.0, 0.4501, 0.005)
rng = {}; lines = ['T_K\tphase\tcalc_ylow\tcalc_yhigh\tn_points']
for T in TS:
    fr = {'TAU1': [], 'TAU2': []}
    for y in YS:
        f, _ = frac(ALL, 1/14, 13*y/14, float(T))
        for t in fr:
            if f.get(t, 0) >= 0.98: fr[t].append(round(float(y), 3))
    for t, ys in fr.items():
        rng[(T, t)] = (min(ys), max(ys)) if ys else None
        lines.append(f'{T}\t{t}\t{min(ys) if ys else ""}\t{max(ys) if ys else ""}\t{len(ys)}'); print(lines[-1], flush=True)
open(out + '_ranges.tsv', 'w').write('\n'.join(lines) + '\n')
# descriptor D(x,T)
Dl = ['T_K\tx\tD_J_per_molatom']
D = {}
for Tc, Tk in ((1050, 1323.15), (1150, 1423.15), (1200, 1473.15)):
    for x in (1.2, 1.4, 1.6, 1.8, 2.0):
        _, ga = frac(ALL, 1/14, x/14, Tk, 2000); _, gc = frac(COMP, 1/14, x/14, Tk, 2000)
        D[(Tk, x)] = gc - ga; Dl.append(f'{Tk}\t{x}\t{gc-ga:.1f}'); print(Dl[-1], flush=True)
open(out + '_D.tsv', 'w').write('\n'.join(Dl) + '\n')
-e

    for a in ('5','3','6'):
        xla,xfe,xsi=t.nom[a]
        eq=equilibrium(db,['LA','FE','SI','VA'],list(db.phases),{v.X('LA'):xla,v.X('SI'):xsi,v.T:1373,v.P:101325,v.N:1},calc_opts={'pdens':500})
        g=float(eq.GM.values.ravel()[0])
        out=[]
        for p in ('TAU3','TAU4','TAU5','TAU6'):
            c=calculate(db,['LA','FE','SI','VA'],p,T=1373,P=101325,N=1,pdens=2000)
            gm=c.GM.values.ravel(); X=c.X.sel(component='LA').values.ravel()
            out.append(f'{p}:Gmin={gm.min()/1000:.1f}kJ@xLa={X[gm.argmin()]:.2f}')
        print(f'  alloy {a} x={t.nom[a]} Geq={g/1000:.1f}  ',' '.join(out))

 'TAU4':({'FE:SI':'-53021.2027-16*T','SI:FE':'-32022.4058-10.01*T','FE:FE':f'{s4:+d}-5.002*T','SI:SI':'-40016.0024-8.0032*T'},'-171189.014+10*T'),
 'TAU5':({'FE:SI':f'{s5:+d}-13.6*T','SI:FE':'-20002-5.005*T','FE:FE':'15000+15*T','SI:SI':'8000.800-17.50175*T'},'-13000+5*T'),
 'TAU6':({'FE:SI':'-67855-11*T','SI:FE':'20004+10*T','FE:FE':'20008.012-15*T','SI:SI':'-49009-20*T'},f'{l6:+.1f}+10*T')}
GH={'LA':'GHSERLA#','FE':'GHSERFE#','SI':'GHSERSI#'}
def block(name,hyp,sign):
    x,y,z=SITES[name]; n=x+y+z; ends,L=endm(sign)[name]
    out=[f'PHASE {name} % 3 {x} {y} {z} !',f'CONSTITUENT {name} : LA : FE,SI : FE,SI : !']
    for key,val in ends.items():
        i,j=key.split(':'); ref=f'+{x}*{GH["LA"]}+{y}*{GH[i]}+{z}*{GH[j]}'
        expr={'A':f'+{val}','B':f'+{val}{ref}','E':f'+{n}*({val}){ref}'}[hyp]
        out.append(f' PARAMETER G({name},LA:{i}:{j};0) 298.15 {expr}; 6000 N !')
    Lx=f'+{n}*({L})' if hyp=='E' else f'+{L}'
    for ca in ('LA:FE,SI:FE','LA:FE,SI:SI','LA:FE:FE,SI','LA:SI:FE,SI','LA:FE,SI:FE,SI'):
        out.append(f' PARAMETER L({name},{ca};0) 298.15 {Lx}; 6000 N !')
    return '\n'.join(out)
MAP={'LA5SIFE3':'La5Si3','LA3SIFE2':'La3Si2','LA5SIFE4':'La5Si4','LASIFE':'LaSi','ALASIFE2':'alpha-LaSi2','BLASIFE2':'beta-LaSi2','FE2SI':'Fe2Si','FE5SI3':'Fe5Si3','FESI_B20':'FeSi','BCC_A2':'bcc','FCC_A1':'fcc','LIQUID':'liquid','FESI2_H':'FeSi2','FESI2_L':'FeSi2','DIAMOND_A4':'Si','TAU1':'tau1','TAU2':'tau2','TAU3':'tau3','TAU4':'tau4','TAU5':'tau5','TAU6':'tau6'}
def norm(s): return frozenset('bcc' if p in('alpha-Fe','B2','D03') else p for p in re.split(r'\s*\+\s*',s.strip()))
bench={r['alloy']:(norm(r['experimental']),norm(r['calculated'])) for r in csv.DictReader(open(T6))}
nom={}
for r in csv.DictReader(open(T4)):
    m=re.match(r'La(\d+)Fe(\d+)Si(\d+)',r['nominal']); nom[r['alloy']]=tuple(int(g)/100 for g in m.groups())
def run(hyp,sign,withtau=True):
    txt=open(BASE).read()
    if withtau: txt+='\n'+'\n'.join(block(n,hyp,sign) for n in SITES)
    open('/tmp/tau_test.tdb','w').write(txt); db=Database('/tmp/tau_test.tdb'); ph=list(db.phases)
    res={}
    for a,(xla,xfe,xsi) in nom.items():
        try:
            eq=equilibrium(db,['LA','FE','SI','VA'],ph,{v.X('LA'):xla,v.X('SI'):xsi,v.T:1373,v.P:101325,v.N:1},calc_opts={'pdens':500})
            res[a]=frozenset(MAP.get(str(p),str(p)) for p,n in zip(np.array(eq.Phase).ravel(),np.array(eq.NP).ravel()) if str(p) not in('','nan') and not np.isnan(n) and n>0.01)
        except Exception as e: res[a]=frozenset(['FAIL'])
    return res
def score(res):
    ex=sum(res[a]==bench[a][0] for a in res); fc=sum(res[a]==bench[a][1] for a in res)
    jx=np.mean([len(res[a]&bench[a][0])/len(res[a]|bench[a][0]) for a in res]); jf=np.mean([len(res[a]&bench[a][1])/len(res[a]|bench[a][1]) for a in res])
    tau=lambda s:{p for p in s if p in('tau3','tau4','tau5','tau6')}
    t_ex=sum(1 for a in res if tau(bench[a][0]) and tau(bench[a][0])<=res[a]); n_ex=sum(1 for a in res if tau(bench[a][0]))
    return ex,fc,jx,jf,t_ex,n_ex
if __name__=='__main__':
    out={}
    for label,hyp,sign,wt in (('no tau3-6','-','NEW',False),)+tuple((f'{h} {s}',h,s,True) for s in('OLD','NEW') for h in('A','B','E')):
        res=run(hyp,sign,wt); out[label]=res; ex,fc,jx,jf,t,n=score(res)
        print(f'{label:10s} exact vs experiment {ex:2d}/21  exact vs Feng-calc {fc:2d}/21  Jaccard exp {jx:.2f} calc {jf:.2f}  tau3-6 found where reported {t}/{n}',flush=True)
    import json; json.dump({k:{a:sorted(v_) for a,v_ in r.items()} for k,r in out.items()},open('/home/claude/tau36_rerun.json','w'))

"""
audit.py — validate the reconstructed TDB against the frozen acceptance
test (FROZEN_SPEC.md §4) and compute the WP4 descriptor.

  python audit.py            # runs A1-A5, computes dG_f, writes the section plot
"""
import os
import numpy as np
import sympy
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pycalphad import Database, equilibrium, variables as v

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
TDB = os.path.join(HERE, 'LaFeSi_feng2023.tdb')
T = sympy.Symbol('T')
COMPS = ['LA', 'FE', 'SI', 'VA']
XLA, XFE, XSI = 1/14, 11.5/14, 1.5/14          # frozen La(Fe11.5Si1.5)
UNARY_REF = {'GHSERLA': [-70980.2, -119873.4], 'GHSERFE': [-41450.4, -80562.9],
             'GHSERSI': [-30381.7, -56966.0]}


def stable(db, phases, xLa, xSi, Tk=1373, thr=0.01):
    eq = equilibrium(db, COMPS, phases,
                     {v.X('LA'): xLa, v.X('SI'): xSi, v.T: Tk, v.P: 101325, v.N: 1},
                     calc_opts={'pdens': 2000})
    ph = np.array(eq.Phase).ravel()
    npf = np.array(eq.NP).ravel()
    out = {}
    for p, n in zip(ph, npf):
        if p and str(p) not in ('nan', '') and not np.isnan(n) and n > thr:
            out[str(p)] = out.get(str(p), 0.0) + float(n)
    return out, float(np.array(eq.GM).ravel()[0])


def main():
    db = Database(TDB)
    phases = list(db.phases.keys())
    print(f"A1 parse+compute: {len(phases)} phases loaded")

    print("\nA2 unary consistency (numeric, 1000/1500 K):")
    for n, exp in UNARY_REF.items():
        got = [round(float(sympy.sympify(db.symbols[n]).xreplace({T: TT})), 1) for TT in (1000, 1500)]
        print(f"   {n}: {got} {'OK' if got == exp else 'MISMATCH'}")

    print("\nA3 tau1 at frozen point La(Fe11.5Si1.5) 1373 K:")
    d, gm = stable(db, phases, XLA, XSI)
    print(f"   {d}  -> {'PASS' if d.get('TAU1', 0) > 0.99 else 'CHECK'}")

    print("\nA4 Feng Table 4 tau1-bearing alloys:")
    feng = {10: (9, 66, 25, 'tau3,tau1'), 11: (7, 78, 15, 'tau1,aFe,tau5'),
            13: (7, 71, 22, 'tau1,tau2,tau3'), 17: (6, 75, 19, 'tau1,aFe'),
            21: (9, 71, 20, 'tau3,tau1')}
    for a, (la, fe, si, rep) in feng.items():
        d, _ = stable(db, phases, la/100, si/100)
        print(f"   #{a}: reported[{rep}] computed[{', '.join(sorted(d))}]")

    print("\nA5 tau1/tau2 window along La(Fe1-xSix)13, 1373 K (lit: tau1 0.096-0.229, tau2 0.266+):")
    for xs in [0.08, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.23, 0.27, 0.30]:
        d, _ = stable(db, phases, 1/14, (13*xs)/14)
        print(f"   x={xs:.2f}: {', '.join(f'{k}:{v:.2f}' for k, v in sorted(d.items()))}")

    print("\nWP4 descriptor dG_f(tau1) at La(Fe11.5Si1.5) vs SER elements:")
    for Tann in (1173, 1273, 1373, 1473):
        d, gm = stable(db, phases, XLA, XSI, Tann)
        gser = {n: float(sympy.sympify(db.symbols[n]).xreplace({T: Tann}))
                for n in ('GHSERLA', 'GHSERFE', 'GHSERSI')}
        ref = XLA*gser['GHSERLA'] + XFE*gser['GHSERFE'] + XSI*gser['GHSERSI']
        single = 'TAU1' if d.get('TAU1', 0) > 0.99 else '+'.join(sorted(d))
        print(f"   T={Tann}K: dG_f={gm-ref:9.1f} J/mol-atom   ({single})")

    section_plot(db, phases)


def section_plot(db, phases, Tk=1373):
    sq3 = 3 ** 0.5 / 2
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 7))
    labels = {}
    step = 0.035
    for xfe in np.arange(0.02, 0.98, step):
        for xsi in np.arange(0.02, 0.98 - xfe, step):
            xla = 1 - xfe - xsi
            if xla < 0.01:
                continue
            d, _ = stable(db, phases, xla, xsi, Tk, thr=0.02)
            key = '+'.join(sorted(d))
            labels.setdefault(key, []).append((xsi + xla/2, xla*sq3))
    cmap = plt.get_cmap('tab20', max(len(labels), 1))
    for i, (key, pts) in enumerate(sorted(labels.items())):
        xs, ys = zip(*pts)
        ax.scatter(xs, ys, s=16, color=cmap(i), label=key[:42] or 'none')
    ax.plot([0, 1, 0.5, 0], [0, 0, sq3, 0], 'k-', lw=1.2)
    for (x, y), t in (((-0.03, -0.03), 'Fe'), ((1.01, -0.03), 'Si'), ((0.5, sq3+0.02), 'La')):
        ax.text(x, y, t, fontsize=13, weight='bold')
    ax.set_title(f'La-Fe-Si {Tk} K, reconstructed from Feng et al. (2023)\n'
                 'tau1/tau2 + solution + compounds (tau3-tau6 deferred)', fontsize=9)
    ax.legend(fontsize=5, loc='upper right', ncol=2)
    ax.set_aspect('equal')
    ax.axis('off')
    fig.tight_layout()
    out = os.path.join(HERE, f'section_{Tk}K.png')
    fig.savefig(out, dpi=130)
    print(f"\nwrote {out}")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
-e

---
# Binary collection — validation (Track A lessons applied)

Source: `iliya-radulov/projects_documentation` → `AlloyDB/Data/tdb/sgte_binary/`.
The La–Fe–Si subset: 2 FeLa × 2 LaSi × 5 FeSi = **20 ternary combinations**.

## Feng's cited binaries are all present
Feng et al. (2023) optimised the ternary on: La–Si = Zhou 2010 [20],
Fe–Si = Cui 2017 [23], La–Fe = Su 2022 [24]. The collection has
**`LaSi-10Zho`, `FeSi-17Cui`, `FeLa-23Su`** — so a faithful merged
reconstruction (ternary params on the exact cited binaries) is possible,
not just the self-contained one.

## Lessons 1 & 2 — all pass (`check_binaries.py`)
- **Standalone compute:** all 9 binary files load and compute in pycalphad.
- **3rd-generation screen:** none use Einstein/3rd-gen unaries — including
  the 2020s files `FeLa-23Su`, `LaSi-20Xu`, `FeSi-23Wit`. All 2nd-gen SGTE.
- **Unary consistency (numeric, not text):** GHSERLA, GHSERFE, GHSERSI each
  take **one distinct value** across every file (−119873.4 / −80562.9 /
  −56966.0 at 1500 K), and match the self-contained TDB's unaries exactly.

## Faithfulness of the self-contained TDB vs the real cited binaries
Liquid Gibbs energy of mixing at x=0.5, 1873 K (`crosscheck_binaries.py`):

| system | real cited binary | my typed Feng T5 | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| La–Si (LaSi-10Zho) | −91932.3 | −91932.3 | **exact** |
| La–Fe (FeLa-23Su) | −4948.5 | −4948.5 | **exact** |
| Fe–Si (FeSi-17Cui) | −37367.1 | −36828.1 | −539 (1.4%) |

So the self-contained reconstruction is **exactly faithful for La–Si and
La–Fe**, and within 1.4% on the Fe–Si liquid (Feng's Table 5 slightly
rounds/simplifies Cui's Fe–Si liquid RK terms). The real `FeSi-17Cui` also
carries the full Fe–Si **B2/D03 ordering** (A2_BCC/B2_BCC/BCC_4SL) that the
self-contained build deferred.

## Next: merged reconstruction + WP4 band
- Merge Feng's 3 cited binaries + the typed ternary fragment → the exact
  faithful TDB, with B2/D03. Validate against the same acceptance test.
- WP4 uncertainty band: build all 20 merged ternaries (swap the binaries)
  and compute the τ1 formation driving force ΔG* at La(Fe11.5Si1.5),
  T_anneal — the honest band on the descriptor.
-e

"""check_binaries.py — standalone-compute, 3rd-gen screen, and numeric unary
consistency for the La-Fe-Si binary collection (Track A lessons 1 & 2)."""
import sys, os, re, glob, warnings
warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
import sympy
from pycalphad import Database, calculate
T = sympy.Symbol('T')
BINDIR = sys.argv[1]
files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(BINDIR, 'FeLa-*.tdb')) +
               glob.glob(os.path.join(BINDIR, 'LaSi-*.tdb')) +
               glob.glob(os.path.join(BINDIR, 'FeSi-*.tdb')))
unary = {}
print(f"{'file':20s} {'elems':12s} {'phases':3s} compute 3rdgen  GHSERLA/FE/SI(1500K)")
for f in files:
    name = os.path.basename(f)
    txt = open(f, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
    gen3 = 'yes' if re.search(r'EINSTEIN|GEIN', txt, re.I) else 'no'
    try:
        db = Database(f)
        els = sorted(e for e in db.elements if e not in ('/-', 'VA'))
        # standalone compute: GM of first non-trivial phase
        ok = 'ok'
        try:
            ph = [p for p in db.phases if 'LIQ' in p.upper()] or list(db.phases)[:1]
            calculate(db, els + ['VA'], ph[0], T=1500, P=101325, output='GM')
        except Exception as e:
            ok = 'FAIL'
        vals = {}
        for u in ('GHSERLA', 'GHSERFE', 'GHSERSI'):
            s = db.symbols.get(u)
            if s is not None:
                vals[u] = round(float(sympy.sympify(s).xreplace({T: 1500})), 1)
                unary.setdefault(u, {})[name] = vals[u]
        vstr = ' '.join(f"{u[-2:]}:{vals.get(u,'--')}" for u in ('GHSERLA','GHSERFE','GHSERSI'))
        print(f"{name:20s} {','.join(els):12s} {len(db.phases):3d} {ok:7s} {gen3:6s}  {vstr}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"{name:20s} PARSE FAIL: {str(e)[:40]}")
print("\nUnary consistency across files (distinct values per function at 1500K):")
for u, d in unary.items():
    vals = sorted(set(d.values()))
    print(f"  {u}: {len(vals)} distinct value(s) -> {vals}")
    if len(vals) > 1:
        for v in vals:
            print(f"     {v}: {[n for n,x in d.items() if x==v]}")

"""crosscheck_binaries.py — compare the self-contained TDB's typed binary
parameters against the real cited binaries (faithfulness proof).
Usage: python crosscheck_binaries.py <binary_tdb_dir>"""
import sys, warnings; warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')
import numpy as np
from pycalphad import Database, calculate
BIN = sys.argv[1].rstrip('/') + '/'
mine = Database(sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else
                __file__.rsplit('/tdb_build/', 1)[0] + '/tdb_build/LaFeSi_feng2023.tdb')

def gmix_liquid(db, elA, elB, T=1873):
    g = float(np.array(calculate(db, [elA, elB, 'VA'] if 'VA' in db.elements else [elA, elB],
              'LIQUID', T=T, P=101325, points=np.array([[0.5, 0.5]]), output='GM').GM).ravel()[0])
    gA = float(np.array(calculate(db, [elA, elB], 'LIQUID', T=T, P=101325,
              points=np.array([[1.0, 0.0]]), output='GM').GM).ravel()[0])
    gB = float(np.array(calculate(db, [elA, elB], 'LIQUID', T=T, P=101325,
              points=np.array([[0.0, 1.0]]), output='GM').GM).ravel()[0])
    return g - 0.5 * gA - 0.5 * gB

for sysname, (elA, elB, f) in {'Fe-Si': ('FE', 'SI', 'FeSi-17Cui.tdb'),
                               'La-Si': ('LA', 'SI', 'LaSi-10Zho.tdb'),
                               'La-Fe': ('LA', 'FE', 'FeLa-23Su.tdb')}.items():
    gr = gmix_liquid(Database(BIN + f), elA, elB)
    gm = gmix_liquid(mine, elA, elB)
    print(f"{sysname}: real[{f}]={gr:.1f}  mine={gm:.1f}  delta={gm-gr:+.1f} J/mol")
-e

---
"""
build_merged_tdb.py — FULL MERGED build: real binary TDBs + Feng ternary.

Merges three binary TDB files (Fe-La, La-Si, Fe-Si) from the Track A SGTE
collection into one La-Fe-Si database, then injects Feng et al. (2023)
Table 5 ternary parameters (tau1/tau2 = La(Fe,Si)13 and the ternary liquid
interaction). The binary backbone is the real research files, not Feng's
Table-5 restatement — so this is the reconstruction on actual binaries, and
swapping the inputs gives the WP4 uncertainty band.

Faithful combo = Feng's cited binaries: FeLa-23Su (Su), LaSi-10Zho (Zhou),
FeSi-17Cui (Cui). Fe-Si is merged DISORDERED (BCC_A2 + line compounds):
Feng themselves treated Fe-Si as A2 for the ternary and added B2/D03
separately (paper p.9), so Cui's 4SL ordering phases are left out of the
ternary merge.

  python build_merged_tdb.py FeLa-23Su LaSi-10Zho FeSi-17Cui [out.tdb]
"""
import os
import sys
import copy

from pycalphad import Database

COLL = '/home/user/projects_documentation/AlloyDB/Data/tdb/sgte_binary'
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SKIP_PHASES = {'A2_BCC', 'B2_BCC', 'BCC_4SL'}      # Cui ordering: added separately, as Feng did

# Feng Table 5 ternary additions (tau1/tau2 model (La)0.071428(Fe,Si)0.928572)
FENG_TERNARY = """
$ ===== Feng et al. (2023) Table 5 -- ternary additions on the merged binaries =====
 PARAMETER G(LIQUID,LA,FE,SI;0) 298.15 +200000; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 THIS WORK

PHASE TAU1 % 2 0.071428 0.928572 !
CONSTITUENT TAU1 : LA : FE,SI : !
 PARAMETER G(TAU1,LA:FE;0) 298.15 +2300-0.95*T+0.071428*GHSERLA#+0.928572*GHSERFE#; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5
 PARAMETER G(TAU1,LA:SI;0) 298.15 +37000+6.5*T+0.071428*GHSERLA#+0.928572*GHSERSI#; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5
 PARAMETER G(TAU1,LA:FE,SI;0) 298.15 -242114+9.5*T; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5

PHASE TAU2 % 2 0.071428 0.928572 !
CONSTITUENT TAU2 : LA : FE,SI : !
 PARAMETER G(TAU2,LA:FE;0) 298.15 +6500-0.9*T+0.071428*GHSERLA#+0.928572*GHSERFE#; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5
 PARAMETER G(TAU2,LA:SI;0) 298.15 +22500+8.5*T+0.071428*GHSERLA#+0.928572*GHSERSI#; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5
 PARAMETER G(TAU2,LA:FE,SI;0) 298.15 -241114+8*T; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5
"""


def merge_binaries(paths):
    """Object-level merge: union elements/symbols/phases/parameters.
    Shared solution phases get their constituent sets unioned per sublattice."""
    merged = Database()
    merged.elements = set()
    for path in paths:
        db = Database(path)
        merged.elements |= set(db.elements)
        # symbols (unary functions): dedup by name; verified consistent upstream
        for name, expr in db.symbols.items():
            merged.symbols.setdefault(name, expr)
        # phases
        for pname, phase in db.phases.items():
            if pname in SKIP_PHASES:
                continue
            if pname not in merged.phases:
                merged.phases[pname] = copy.deepcopy(phase)
            else:
                # union constituents per sublattice
                old = merged.phases[pname]
                if len(old.constituents) == len(phase.constituents):
                    old.constituents = tuple(
                        frozenset(a | b) for a, b in zip(old.constituents, phase.constituents))
        # parameters: union (skip ones for skipped phases)
        for p in db._parameters.all():
            if p['phase_name'] in SKIP_PHASES:
                continue
            merged._parameters.insert(dict(p))
    return merged


def build(fela, lasi, fesi, out=None):
    paths = [os.path.join(COLL, f + '.tdb') for f in (fela, lasi, fesi)]
    merged = merge_binaries(paths)
    backbone = merged.to_string(fmt='tdb')
    tdb_text = backbone + '\n' + FENG_TERNARY + '\n'
    out = out or os.path.join(HERE, f'merged_{fela}_{lasi}_{fesi}.tdb')
    open(out, 'w').write(tdb_text)
    # reload to confirm it parses with the ternary
    db = Database(out)
    return out, db


if __name__ == '__main__':
    args = sys.argv[1:]
    fela, lasi, fesi = (args + ['FeLa-23Su', 'LaSi-10Zho', 'FeSi-17Cui'])[:3]
    out = args[3] if len(args) > 3 else None
    path, db = build(fela, lasi, fesi, out)
    print(f'wrote {path}')
    print(f'elements: {sorted(e for e in db.elements if e not in ("VA", "/-"))}')
    print(f'{len(db.phases)} phases: {sorted(db.phases)}')
-e

# FILE: stage_four/calphad_lafesi/tdb_build/build_tdb.py
---
"""
build_tdb.py — assemble a La–Fe–Si TDB from Feng et al. (2023) Table 5.

Reconstruction (no author TDB). Unaries: SGTE / Dinsdale 1991, extracted
verbatim from pycalphad-bundled databases and numerically verified to agree
across sources (see FROZEN_SPEC.md §1). Ternary + binary-excess + compound
parameters: typed from Feng Table 5 (data_feng2023/table5_parameters.md),
each block carrying a provenance comment.

Feng's Gibbs energies are PER MOLE OF ATOMS (the GHSER coefficients sum to
1), so each phase's sublattice site ratios ARE those coefficients.

This version builds the fully-specified subset: LIQUID, FCC_A1, BCC_A2,
DIAMOND_A4, the Fe–Si line compounds, the six La–Si(Fe) compounds, and the
ternary tau1/tau2 = La(Fe,Si)13. tau3–tau6 and the Fe–Si B2/D03 ordering
are deferred (FROZEN_SPEC §3, §4).

  python build_tdb.py            # writes LaFeSi_feng2023.tdb and validates
"""
import os
import glob
import re

import pycalphad

PCDIR = os.path.dirname(pycalphad.__file__)
HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
OUT = os.path.join(HERE, 'LaFeSi_feng2023.tdb')


def find(fname):
    return glob.glob(PCDIR + '/**/' + fname, recursive=True)[0]


def extract_function(path, name):
    """Verbatim FUNCTION block body (between name and the terminating !)."""
    txt = open(path, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()
    m = re.search(r'FUNCTION\s+' + name + r'\b(.*?)!', txt, re.S | re.I)
    if not m:
        raise KeyError(f'{name} not in {os.path.basename(path)}')
    return re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', m.group(1)).strip()


# --- unary function sources (all verified SGTE/Dinsdale, FROZEN_SPEC §1) ---
FENDB = os.path.join(HERE, '..', '..', '..', 'stage_three', 'FENDB_merged_v4.tdb')
SRC = {
    'GHSERLA': find('zrlayalo.tdb'), 'GLABCC': find('zrlayalo.tdb'),
    'GLAFCC': find('zrlayalo.tdb'), 'GLALIQ': find('zrlayalo.tdb'),
    'GHSERFE': FENDB, 'GFCCFE': FENDB, 'GLIQFE': find('CrFeNb_Jacob2016.tdb'),
    'GHSERSI': find('COST507.tdb'), 'GSIBCC': find('mc_fecocrnbti.tdb'),
    'GSIFCC': find('mc_fecocrnbti.tdb'),
}
# liquid Si typed from COST507's LIQUID,SI parameter (verified canonical)
GLIQSI_BODY = ('298.15 +50696.4-30.0994*T+2.09307E-21*T**7+GHSERSI#; '
               '1687.00 Y +49828.2-29.5591*T+4.20369E+30*T**(-9)+GHSERSI#; 6000.00 N')


def unary_block():
    lines = ['$ ===== SGTE / Dinsdale 1991 unary functions '
             '(verbatim; verified across sources, FROZEN_SPEC §1) =====']
    # fix cross-references: FENDB names the bcc/fcc Fe stabilities GHSERFE/GFCCFE
    for name in ('GHSERLA', 'GLABCC', 'GLAFCC', 'GLALIQ',
                 'GHSERFE', 'GFCCFE', 'GLIQFE',
                 'GHSERSI', 'GSIBCC', 'GSIFCC'):
        body = extract_function(SRC[name], name)
        lines.append(f'FUNCTION {name} {body} !')
    lines.append(f'FUNCTION GLIQSI {GLIQSI_BODY} !')
    # convenience aliases matching Feng's Table-5 notation
    lines.append('$ Feng notation: GHCP_La = dhcp-La SER = GHSERLA; '
                 'GDIA_Si = diamond-Si SER = GHSERSI; GBCC_Fe = bcc-Fe SER = GHSERFE')
    return '\n'.join(lines)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Feng Table 5 parameters  (energies J/mol-atom; provenance per block)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
HEADER = """$ ============================================================
$ La-Fe-Si -- reconstruction of Feng et al., Calphad 83 (2023) 102643
$ Ternary + binary-excess parameters typed from the paper's Table 5.
$ Unaries: SGTE/Dinsdale 1991 (see build_tdb.py, FROZEN_SPEC.md).
$ Scope: LIQUID, FCC_A1, BCC_A2, DIAMOND_A4, Fe-Si compounds,
$        La-Si(Fe) compounds, tau1/tau2 = La(Fe,Si)13.
$ Deferred: tau3-tau6, Fe-Si B2/D03 ordering.
$ ============================================================
ELEMENT VA   VACUUM               0.0      0.0      0.0    !
ELEMENT LA   DOUBLE_HCP(ABAC)   138.9055  6667.0   57.488 !
ELEMENT FE   BCC_A2              55.847    4489.0   27.28  !
ELEMENT SI   DIAMOND_A4          28.0855   3217.0   18.81  !

TYPE_DEFINITION % SEQ * !
DEFINE_SYSTEM_DEFAULT ELEMENT 2 !
DEFAULT_COMMAND DEFINE_SYSTEM_ELEMENT VA !

TYPE_DEFINITION & GES AMEND_PHASE_DESCRIPTION BCC_A2 MAGNETIC -1.0 0.4 !
TYPE_DEFINITION ) GES AMEND_PHASE_DESCRIPTION FCC_A1 MAGNETIC -3.0 0.28 !
"""

# site ratios = Feng's per-atom GHSER coefficients
LASI_COMPOUNDS = [
    # (phase, La_ratio, Si_ratio, G_La:Si, G_La:Fe, L_La:Si,Fe)
    ('LA5SIFE3', 0.625, 0.375,
     '-60012.5-14.37*T+0.625*GHSERLA#+0.375*GHSERSI#',
     '+8001.1109+8.001*T+0.625*GHSERLA#+0.375*GHSERFE#',
     '-25999.4388+4.9996*T'),
    ('LA3SIFE2', 0.6, 0.4,
     '-63125.4-14.93*T+0.6*GHSERLA#+0.4*GHSERSI#',
     '+10000+11*T+0.6*GHSERLA#+0.4*GHSERFE#',
     '-26500+5*T'),
    ('LA5SIFE4', 0.5556, 0.4444,
     '-67018.6-15.43*T+0.5556*GHSERLA#+0.4444*GHSERSI#',
     '+5000+9*T+0.5556*GHSERLA#+0.4444*GHSERFE#',
     '+36500+7.5*T'),
    ('LASIFE', 0.5, 0.5,
     '-70156.2-15.4*T+0.5*GHSERLA#+0.5*GHSERSI#',
     '+8000+10*T+0.5*GHSERLA#+0.5*GHSERFE#',
     '-43500+6.5*T'),
    ('ALASIFE2', 0.36, 0.64,
     '-53051.2-21.49*T+0.36*GHSERLA#+0.64*GHSERSI#',
     '+8900+8*T+0.36*GHSERLA#+0.64*GHSERFE#',
     '-115863.005+9*T'),
    ('BLASIFE2', 0.3333, 0.6667,
     '-49262.3-21.048*T+0.3333*GHSERLA#+0.6667*GHSERSI#',
     '+9504.75086+10*T+0.3333*GHSERLA#+0.6667*GHSERFE#',
     '-1.294+7*T'),
]

# Fe-Si stoichiometric line compounds: (phase, Fe_ratio, Si_ratio, G)
FESI_COMPOUNDS = [
    ('FE2SI', 0.66667, 0.33333, '-30592.9+0.33333*GHSERSI#+0.66667*GHSERFE#'),
    ('FE5SI3', 0.625, 0.375, '-34224.6+1.53653*T+0.375*GHSERSI#+0.625*GHSERFE#'),
    ('FESI_B20', 0.5, 0.5, '-39705.0+2.08759*T+0.5*GHSERSI#+0.5*GHSERFE#'),
    ('FESI2_L', 0.333, 0.667, '-39571.0+10.6912*T+0.6667*GHSERSI#+0.333*GHSERFE#'),
    ('FESI2_H', 0.3, 0.7, '-23969.4+0.7*GHSERSI#+0.3*GHSERFE#'),
]


def phases_and_params():
    L = []
    # ----- LIQUID (La,Fe,Si)1 -----
    L.append('$ ----- LIQUID -----')
    L.append('PHASE LIQUID % 1 1.0 !')
    L.append('CONSTITUENT LIQUID : LA,FE,SI : !')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(LIQUID,LA;0) 298.15 +GLALIQ#; 6000 N ! $ unary')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(LIQUID,FE;0) 298.15 +GLIQFE#; 6000 N ! $ unary')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(LIQUID,SI;0) 298.15 +GLIQSI#; 6000 N ! $ unary')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(LIQUID,LA,FE;0) 298.15 +19054.390+2.3114202*T; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [24]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(LIQUID,LA,FE;1) 298.15 +22910.538-10.052670*T; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [24]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(LIQUID,LA,FE;2) 298.15 +8497.879; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [24]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(LIQUID,LA,SI;0) 298.15 -249912.5-39.85*T; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [20]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(LIQUID,LA,SI;1) 298.15 +25123.5; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [20]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(LIQUID,LA,SI;2) 298.15 +83012.5; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [20]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(LIQUID,LA,SI;3) 298.15 -21695.6; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [20]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(LIQUID,FE,SI;0) 298.15 -150802.2+24.9159*T; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [23]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(LIQUID,FE,SI;1) 298.15 -22532.7; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [23]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(LIQUID,FE,SI;2) 298.15 +23530.4; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [23]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(LIQUID,LA,FE,SI;0) 298.15 +200000; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 THIS WORK')

    # ----- FCC_A1 (La,Fe,Si)1(Va)1 -----
    L.append('$ ----- FCC_A1 -----')
    L.append('PHASE FCC_A1 %) 2 1 1 !')
    L.append('CONSTITUENT FCC_A1 : LA,FE,SI : VA : !')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(FCC_A1,LA:VA;0) 298.15 +GLAFCC#; 6000 N ! $ unary')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(FCC_A1,FE:VA;0) 298.15 +GFCCFE#; 6000 N ! $ unary')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(FCC_A1,SI:VA;0) 298.15 +GSIFCC#; 6000 N ! $ unary')
    L.append(' PARAMETER TC(FCC_A1,FE:VA;0) 298.15 -201; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [23]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER BMAGN(FCC_A1,FE:VA;0) 298.15 -2.1; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [23]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(FCC_A1,LA,FE:VA;0) 298.15 +60142.574-9.7517685*T; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [24]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(FCC_A1,LA,SI:VA;0) 298.15 -191235.4; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [20]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(FCC_A1,FE,SI:VA;0) 298.15 -167164.9+42.9734*T; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [23]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(FCC_A1,FE,SI:VA;1) 298.15 -44950.4; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [23]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(FCC_A1,FE,SI:VA;2) 298.15 +19706.6; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [23]')

    # ----- BCC_A2 (La,Fe,Si)1(Va)3 -----
    L.append('$ ----- BCC_A2 -----')
    L.append('PHASE BCC_A2 %& 2 1 3 !')
    L.append('CONSTITUENT BCC_A2 : LA,FE,SI : VA : !')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(BCC_A2,LA:VA;0) 298.15 +GLABCC#; 6000 N ! $ unary')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(BCC_A2,FE:VA;0) 298.15 +GHSERFE#; 6000 N ! $ unary (bcc SER)')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(BCC_A2,SI:VA;0) 298.15 +GSIBCC#; 6000 N ! $ unary')
    L.append(' PARAMETER TC(BCC_A2,FE:VA;0) 298.15 +1043; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [23]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER BMAGN(BCC_A2,FE:VA;0) 298.15 +2.22; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [23]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER TC(BCC_A2,FE,SI:VA;1) 298.15 +504; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [23]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER BMAGN(BCC_A2,FE,SI:VA;1) 298.15 +1.07; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [23]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(BCC_A2,LA,FE:VA;0) 298.15 +45319.444; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [24]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(BCC_A2,LA,SI:VA;0) 298.15 -202356.5; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [20]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(BCC_A2,FE,SI:VA;0) 298.15 -180000.0+47.8494*T; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [23]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(BCC_A2,FE,SI:VA;1) 298.15 -32198.0; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [23]')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(BCC_A2,FE,SI:VA;2) 298.15 +15882.8; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [23]')

    # ----- DIAMOND_A4 (Si) -----
    L.append('$ ----- DIAMOND_A4 -----')
    L.append('PHASE DIAMOND_A4 % 1 1.0 !')
    L.append('CONSTITUENT DIAMOND_A4 : SI : !')
    L.append(' PARAMETER G(DIAMOND_A4,SI;0) 298.15 +GHSERSI#; 6000 N ! $ unary (diamond SER)')

    # ----- Fe-Si line compounds -----
    L.append('$ ----- Fe-Si line compounds (Feng T5 [23]) -----')
    for name, rfe, rsi, g in FESI_COMPOUNDS:
        L.append(f'PHASE {name} % 2 {rfe} {rsi} !')
        L.append(f'CONSTITUENT {name} : FE : SI : !')
        L.append(f' PARAMETER G({name},FE:SI;0) 298.15 +{g}; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [23]')

    # ----- La-Si(Fe) compounds: (La)a(Si,Fe)b -----
    L.append('$ ----- La-Si(Fe) compounds (Feng T5 [20] + THIS WORK solubility) -----')
    for name, rla, rx, gsi, gfe, lmix in LASI_COMPOUNDS:
        L.append(f'PHASE {name} % 2 {rla} {rx} !')
        L.append(f'CONSTITUENT {name} : LA : SI,FE : !')
        L.append(f' PARAMETER G({name},LA:SI;0) 298.15 +{gsi}; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 [20]')
        L.append(f' PARAMETER G({name},LA:FE;0) 298.15 +{gfe}; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 THIS WORK')
        L.append(f' PARAMETER G({name},LA:SI,FE;0) 298.15 +{lmix}; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 THIS WORK')

    # ----- tau1, tau2 = La(Fe,Si)13 : (La)0.071428(Fe,Si)0.928572 -----
    L.append('$ ----- tau1 (cubic NaZn13) and tau2 (tetragonal) La(Fe,Si)13 (Feng T5 THIS WORK) -----')
    for name, gfe, gsi, lmix in [
        ('TAU1', '2300-0.95*T+0.071428*GHSERLA#+0.928572*GHSERFE#',
                 '37000+6.5*T+0.071428*GHSERLA#+0.928572*GHSERSI#', '-242114+9.5*T'),
        ('TAU2', '6500-0.9*T+0.071428*GHSERLA#+0.928572*GHSERFE#',
                 '22500+8.5*T+0.071428*GHSERLA#+0.928572*GHSERSI#', '-241114+8*T')]:
        L.append(f'PHASE {name} % 2 0.071428 0.928572 !')
        L.append(f'CONSTITUENT {name} : LA : FE,SI : !')
        L.append(f' PARAMETER G({name},LA:FE;0) 298.15 +{gfe}; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 THIS WORK')
        L.append(f' PARAMETER G({name},LA:SI;0) 298.15 +{gsi}; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 THIS WORK')
        L.append(f' PARAMETER G({name},LA:FE,SI;0) 298.15 +{lmix}; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 THIS WORK')
    return '\n'.join(L)


def build():
    tdb = '\n'.join([HEADER, unary_block(), phases_and_params(), ''])
    open(OUT, 'w').write(tdb)
    print(f'wrote {OUT} ({len(tdb)} bytes)')
    return OUT


if __name__ == '__main__':
    build()
-e

# Frozen build spec — La–Fe–Si TDB reconstruction (write-before-run)

*Frozen 15 November 2026, BEFORE any parameter was typed or any equilibrium
run. Pilot discipline (Track A rule): decide the target and the acceptance
test first, so a sign typo cannot quietly pass.*

## 1. What this is

A **reconstruction** (Lindahl-style, minus the author's file) of the
published assessment **Feng et al., Calphad 83 (2023) 102643**: the
ternary parameters typed from the paper's Table 5 onto a binary backbone.

**Faithfulness decision (the "whose binaries" question).** Feng's Table 5
*restates every binary parameter it used*, with ref tags:
La–Si = Zhou 2010 [20], Fe–Si = Cui 2017 [23], La–Fe = Su 2022 [24].
Therefore the faithful backbone is **Feng's own Table 5**, not an external
binary file — typing Table 5 in full reproduces exactly the description the
ternary τ parameters were fitted on. No hybrid risk. (The separate WP4
"swap the binaries, get an uncertainty band" experiment *does* need the
external binary collection; that is a later layer, see §5.)

**Unaries.** SGTE / Dinsdale 1991, taken from pycalphad's bundled
`zrlayalo.tdb` (La), `COST507.tdb` (Si) and the repo's `FENDB_merged_v4.tdb`
(Fe). GHSERLA cross-checked identical between `zrlayalo.tdb` and
`mc_fecocrnbti.tdb`; **La SER = DOUBLE_HCP (dhcp)**, matching Feng's
`GHCP_La` reference term.

## 2. Frozen composition (the WP4 descriptor point)

The 1:13 point, written down first:

```
La(Fe11.5Si1.5)      total 14 atoms, ratio 1 La : 13 (Fe,Si)
  x_La = 1/14    = 0.071429
  x_Fe = 11.5/14 = 0.821429
  x_Si = 1.5/14  = 0.107143
  (Si fraction of the 13 (Fe,Si) sites: x = 1.5/13 = 0.1154)
```

Primary temperature **T_anneal = 1373 K** (Niitsu: τ1 single-phase forms
completely in 5 days at 1373 K; Feng's section is at 1373 K). The WP4
descriptor is ΔG_f(τ1, T_anneal) at this composition; the band comes from
the binary-swap experiment (§5), not needed for the faithful build.

## 3. Scope of this TDB (and documented omission)

Built from Feng Table 5:
- Solution phases LIQUID, FCC_A1, BCC_A2 (with the ternary interaction terms)
- Fe–Si line compounds (Fe2Si, Fe5Si3, FeSi, LT/HT-FeSi2)
- La–Si(Fe) compounds (La5(Si,Fe)3, La3(Si,Fe)2, La5(Si,Fe)4, La(Si,Fe),
  α- and β-La(Si,Fe)2)
- Ternary τ1, τ2 = La(Fe,Si)13 (cubic NaZn13 / tetragonal), model
  (La)(Fe,Si) at 1:13
- Ternary τ3–τ6, model (La)(Si,Fe)(Si,Fe)

**Omitted, on purpose, this version:** the Fe–Si BCC_B2 / D03 ordering
(Cui 2017 4-sublattice). Feng's Table 5 gives only the ΔG anchors for it,
not the full endmember set. B2/D03 matter only in the Fe-rich corner
(Feng alloys #19, #20). Fe–Si there is represented as disordered BCC_A2.
This is a stated limitation, not a silent one: those two alloys are
excluded from the acceptance test below.

## 4. Acceptance test (decided now, before typing)

The build is **accepted** only if all of:

- **A1 — parses & computes.** pycalphad loads the TDB; every phase returns
  finite Gibbs energy over 1000–1700 K; no missing GHSER references.
- **A2 — unary consistency.** GHSERLA, GHSERFE, GHSERSI in the built TDB
  match the SGTE source numerically (not by text) at 300/1000/1700 K.
- **A3 — τ1 is stable at the frozen point.** At La(Fe11.5Si1.5), 1373 K,
  the cubic 1:13 phase τ1 is present in the computed equilibrium.
- **A4 — reproduces Feng's Table 4 (Fe-rich, B2/D03-free subset).** For
  Feng alloys #10, #11, #13, #17, #21 (the τ1-bearing ones), the computed
  stable phase set contains the τ1/τ2/τ3 or αFe phases Feng reports.
  Target: ≥ 4 of 5 qualitatively correct.
- **A5 — τ1 window overlaps the literature.** Along La(Fe1-xSix)13 at
  1373 K, the τ1 single-phase (or τ1-dominant) range overlaps the
  Feng/Niitsu stated 0.096–0.229 in x.

If A1–A3 pass but A4/A5 only partly: **accepted as "computes, partial
match"** — still usable for the WP4 ΔG_f descriptor (A1–A3), with the
phase-boundary caveats logged. A sign typo that breaks A4/A5 while A1–A3
pass is exactly what the per-block provenance comments (§below) are for.

## 5. Later layer — WP4 uncertainty band (needs the external binaries)

Swapping Feng's cited binaries for the other members of the Track A
collection (2 FeLa × 3 LaSi × 5 FeSi) gives the honest uncertainty band on
ΔG_f(τ1, T_anneal). That needs the actual binary TDB files (local
`data/tdb/sgte_binary/`, not in this cloud env). Deferred; the build script
is written to accept an external binary backbone so this is a drop-in later.

## 6. Provenance rule while typing

Every PARAMETER block in the TDB carries a comment: `$ Feng2023 Table5
<phase> <ref>` and any deviation (unit note, suspected typo, correction).
The τ3–τ6 three-sublattice model and the 1:13 site ratio are documented at
the phase definition.
-e

# Full merged build — results

`build_merged_tdb.py` merges three real binary TDBs from the Track A SGTE
collection (`projects_documentation/AlloyDB/Data/tdb/sgte_binary/`) into one
La–Fe–Si database and injects Feng's τ1/τ2 + ternary liquid term.
`wp4_band.py` runs it over all 20 binary combinations.

## Pre-merge checks (Track A lessons)
- **Standalone compute (lesson 1):** all 9 binaries load and compute at
  1373 K. FeSi-23Wit (the flagged Witusiewicz file) computes fine.
- **3rd-gen screen (lesson 2):** all 2nd-generation (no Einstein terms,
  GHSER from 298.15), including the 2020s files FeLa-23Su, LaSi-20Xu,
  FeSi-23Wit.
- **Unary consistency (numeric, not text):** GHSERLA/FE/SI identical across
  all binaries where they overlap, and identical to the self-contained
  build's SGTE source.

## Merge
Shared solution phases (LIQUID, FCC_A1, BCC_A2, …) get their constituents
unioned to (La,Fe,Si); binary interactions and compounds carry over. Cui's
Fe–Si 4-sublattice ordering (A2_BCC/B2_BCC/BCC_4SL) is left out of the
ternary merge — Feng themselves treated Fe–Si as disordered A2 and added
B2/D03 separately (paper p.9). Result: 19 phases, parses and computes.

## The faithfulness proof
The faithful combo (Feng's cited **FeLa-23Su + LaSi-10Zho + FeSi-17Cui**)
reproduces the self-contained Feng-Table-5 build to **< 0.2 J/mol-atom**:

| | self-contained (Table 5) | merged (real binaries) |
|---|---|---|
| ΔG_f(τ1) at 1173 K | −20616.3 | −20616.3 |
| ΔG_f(τ1) at 1373 K | −20992.7 | −20992.6 |
| τ1/τ2 window | 0.10–0.23 / ≥0.27 | identical |

This is the Lindahl criterion: the merge of a set of binaries reproduces an
assessment to < 0.2 J/mol **because the binaries match**. It confirms, two
independent ways, that Feng's Table 5 faithfully restated its binaries and
that our reconstruction is faithful.

## WP4 descriptor and uncertainty band

**Descriptor 1 — ΔG_f(τ1) vs SER elements: binary-independent.** τ1's
energy is Feng's fixed ternary parameters + unaries; the binaries never
enter it. All 20 combinations give −20992.6 J/mol-atom (band = 0). Clean
result: the formation energy of τ1 carries no binary uncertainty.

**Descriptor 2 — τ1 formation driving force** G(competing, τ1/τ2
suspended) − G(τ1): binary-sensitive, the physically meaningful quantity
for whether annealing yields single-phase τ1.

| | driving force [J/mol-atom] | competing assemblage |
|---|---|---|
| 16 of 20 combinations | **+84703** | αFe (BCC_A2) |
| 4 combinations (FeSi-23Wit) | **+82639** | αFe + Fe₂Si |

- τ1 single-phase at the frozen point in **all 20** combinations — the τ1
  window is robust to the binary choice.
- **Band = 2064 J/mol-atom** (~2.5 %), mean 84290 ± 826.
- **The spread is entirely Fe–Si-driven.** The La–Fe (09Pov vs 23Su) and
  La–Si (10Zho vs 20Xu) choices make **zero** difference to the Fe-rich τ1
  descriptor — at this composition the competitor is Fe-based, so only the
  Fe–Si binary matters.
- **FeSi-23Wit (Witusiewicz) is the single outlier**, exactly as flagged:
  its "comprehensive/non-standard" lineage stabilises Fe₂Si as a competitor
  and lowers the driving force by ~2 kJ. An honest, informative band from
  one identifiable assessment, not noise.

## Caveat
With τ1/τ2 suspended, the competing equilibrium at this Fe-rich point is
reported as αFe (± Fe₂Si) with the La-bearing phase below the 0.01 NP
threshold (La is nearly insoluble in αFe; the small La-rich remainder sits
in a trace silicide/liquid). The driving-force magnitude is dominated by
the Fe-rich competitor and the FeSi-23Wit split is robust; the exact
La-partitioning of the trace is not resolved here.

# TDB reconstruction — results

Build: `build_tdb.py` → `LaFeSi_feng2023.tdb`. Validation + descriptor:
`audit.py`. Spec and acceptance test frozen beforehand in `FROZEN_SPEC.md`.

## Acceptance test (FROZEN_SPEC §4) — result: ACCEPTED

| # | test | result |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | parses & computes (17 phases, finite G) | **pass** |
| A2 | GHSERLA/FE/SI match SGTE numerically at 1000/1500 K | **pass** (exact) |
| A3 | τ1 single-phase at the frozen La(Fe11.5Si1.5), 1373 K | **pass** (NP = 1.000) |
| A4 | Feng Table 4 τ1-bearing alloys | τ1 correct in **5/5**; αFe correct where reported (#11, #17); τ3-alloys partial (τ3 deferred) |
| A5 | τ1/τ2 window vs literature | **pass** — τ1 single-phase x≈0.10–0.23, τ2 x≥0.27; lit. τ1 0.096–0.229, τ2 0.266+ |

A1–A3 full; A4/A5 strong with the one documented gap (τ3–τ6 deferred, so
the τ3-bearing alloys #10/#13/#21 substitute another phase for τ3). This
does not touch the τ1 corner or the descriptor.

## WP4 descriptor — ΔG_f(τ1) at La(Fe₁₁.₅Si₁.₅)

Formation Gibbs energy of τ1 relative to the SER elements (dhcp-La,
bcc-Fe, diamond-Si), from the equilibrium GM (τ1 single-phase throughout):

| T (K) | ΔG_f(τ1) [J/mol-atom] |
|---|---|
| 1173 | −20616 |
| 1273 | −20805 |
| **1373 (T_anneal)** | **−20993** |
| 1473 | −21181 |

Nearly linear, ≈ −1.9 J/mol-atom·K, smoothly more negative with T. This is
the Track B physics descriptor ΔG_f*(T_anneal) at the 1:13 composition.

Note: an earlier pass read +23 kJ via `calculate()` on a coarse internal
grid that missed τ1's ideal site occupancy — the equilibrium GM is the
correct source (negative, as a stable phase must be). Logged as a lesson.

## Scope and deferred

Built: LIQUID, FCC_A1, BCC_A2, DIAMOND_A4, the five Fe–Si line compounds,
the six La–Si(Fe) compounds, τ1 and τ2 = La(Fe,Si)₁₃. Deferred (do not
affect the Fe-rich τ1 descriptor): τ3–τ6 (need the three-sublattice site
ratios from a cleaner read of Feng's eq. 8) and the Fe–Si B2/D03 ordering.

## Faithfulness

Binary backbone = Feng's own Table 5 (so the ternary parameters sit on
exactly the binaries they were fitted on — Zhou/Cui/Su; no hybrid). Unaries
SGTE/Dinsdale 1991, verified identical across sources. The separate WP4
uncertainty band (swap Feng's binaries for the Track A collection's other
members) is the next layer and needs those external binary files.

# FILE: stage_four/calphad_lafesi/tdb_build/tau36_block.py
---
"""Generate TDB phase blocks for Feng tau3-tau6 (La)x(Si,Fe)y(Si,Fe)z.

*** NON-VALIDATED. NOT part of the production build. ***
tau3-tau6 could NOT be faithfully reconstructed from Feng (2023): Table 5
omits the GHSER reference terms and the site ratios, and no interpretation
of the printed values reproduces Feng\'s Table 4 / Fig. 5 stabilities. See
TAU36_RECONSTRUCTION.md. This module ships the physically-sensible
hypothesis B (printed + site-weighted GHSER, non-destructive to tau1/tau2)
so the inferred phase definitions are preserved for correction once the
authors\' TDB is obtained. Do NOT use for phase-stability work until
validated.

Reconstruction (Feng Table 5 is incomplete for tau3-tau6: the GHSER
reference terms and the site ratios x,y,z are not printed). Recovered:
- site ratios x,y,z from the Table 4 EPMA compositions (per-atom La frac);
- the printed endmember values are per-FORMULA (magnitude ~ -55000), to
  which the site-weighted SER references are added:
    0G(La:i:j) = printed + x*GHSERLA + y*GHSER_i + z*GHSER_j
  with sublattice-2 = i (y sites), sublattice-3 = j (z sites).
tau6 is NOT in Table 4; its site ratio is a flagged guess (1,2,2).
"""
# phase: (x,y,z, {endmember: printed_value}, L_value)
TAU = {
 'TAU3': (1,2,2, {'FE:SI':'-55000-11.2*T','SI:FE':'-43004.3-10*T',
                  'FE:FE':'10001+8.0032*T','SI:SI':'45000-9*T'}, '-136160.007+5*T'),
 'TAU4': (1,1,2, {'FE:SI':'-53021.2027-16*T','SI:FE':'-32022.4058-10.01*T',
                  'FE:FE':'10001-5.002*T','SI:SI':'-40016.0024-8.0032*T'}, '-171189.014+10*T'),
 'TAU5': (1,1,1, {'FE:SI':'48500-13.6*T','SI:FE':'-20002-5.005*T',
                  'FE:FE':'15000+15*T','SI:SI':'8000.800-17.50175*T'}, '-13000+5*T'),
 'TAU6': (1,2,2, {'FE:SI':'-67855-11*T','SI:FE':'20004+10*T',
                  'FE:FE':'20008.012-15*T','SI:SI':'-49009-20*T'}, '-65006.5+10*T'),
}
GH = {'LA':'GHSERLA#','FE':'GHSERFE#','SI':'GHSERSI#'}

def _ref(x,y,z,i,j):
    # x*La on SL1, y*i on SL2, z*j on SL3
    terms=[f'{x}*{GH["LA"]}'] if x!=1 else [GH['LA']]
    terms.append(f'{y}*{GH[i]}' if y!=1 else GH[i])
    terms.append(f'{z}*{GH[j]}' if z!=1 else GH[j])
    return '+'.join(terms)

def block(name):
    x,y,z,ends,L = TAU[name]
    out=[f'PHASE {name} % 3 {x} {y} {z} !',
         f'CONSTITUENT {name} : LA : FE,SI : FE,SI : !']
    for key,val in ends.items():
        i,j=key.split(':')
        out.append(f' PARAMETER G({name},LA:{i}:{j};0) 298.15 +{val}+{_ref(x,y,z,i,j)}; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5 tau GHSER reconstructed')
    # interaction: all partial + reciprocal equal L (Feng)
    for ca in (f'LA:FE,SI:FE', f'LA:FE,SI:SI', f'LA:FE:FE,SI', f'LA:SI:FE,SI', f'LA:FE,SI:FE,SI'):
        out.append(f' PARAMETER L({name},{ca};0) 298.15 +{L}; 6000 N ! $ Feng T5')
    return '\n'.join(out)

def all_blocks():
    return '\n'.join(block(n) for n in TAU)

if __name__=='__main__':
    print(all_blocks())
-e

# FILE: stage_four/calphad_lafesi/tdb_build/TAU36_RECONSTRUCTION.md
---
# τ3–τ6 reconstruction attempt — finding

**Result: τ3–τ6 cannot be faithfully reconstructed from Feng et al. (2023)
as published.** The production TDB keeps τ1/τ2 only (validated); τ3–τ6 are
documented here and shipped as a flagged, non-validated experiment
(`tau36_block.py`).

## What the paper gives, and what it omits

Eq. 8 defines the model **(La)ₓ(Si,Fe)_y(Si,Fe)_z** with four endmembers
(La:Si:Si, La:Fe:Fe, La:Si:Fe, La:Fe:Si) and reciprocal interactions, per
mole of atoms. Table 5 lists the four endmember "G" values and the
interaction L for each of τ3–τ6, e.g. τ3:
```
G(La:Fe:Si) = -55000 - 11.2*T
G(La:Si:Fe) = -43004.3 - 10*T
G(La:Fe:Fe) = 10001 + 8.0032*T
G(La:Si:Si) = 45000 - 9*T
L(La:Si,Fe:Si,Fe) = -136160.007 + 5*T   (all partial L's equal)
```

**Two things needed to build the phase are not in the paper:**
1. **The GHSER reference terms.** τ1/τ2 print them explicitly
   (`+0.071428·GHSERLA + 0.928572·GHSERFE`); τ3–τ6 print none. Without a
   reference the endmember energy has no absolute level.
2. **The site ratios x, y, z.** Eq. 8 names them but Table 5 does not give
   their values. They were inferred from the Table 4 EPMA compositions:
   τ3 (1,2,2) = LaFe₂Si₂, τ4 (1,1,2) = LaFeSi₂, τ5 (1,1,1) = LaFeSi, τ6
   (1,2,2) [τ6 is not in Table 4 — guess].

## Three reconstructions tested, all against Feng's own Table 4

The acceptance test: do τ3/τ4/τ5 appear in the Table-4 alloys where Feng
reports them, at 1373 K, without breaking the validated τ1/τ2 build?

| hypothesis for the endmember | τ3–τ6 behaviour |
|---|---|
| **A. as printed** (no GHSER) | non-competitive — never stable anywhere |
| **B. printed + site-weighted GHSER** (physically sensible; τ3 ΔG_f ≈ −11 kJ/mol-atom) | too weak — never stable; τ1/τ2 preserved |
| **E. (x+y+z)·printed + GHSER** (τ3 alone looked right) | τ4 super-stable, takes over the whole diagram including the τ1/τ2 window |

None reproduces Feng's Fig. 5 / Table 4 phase stabilities. B is
non-destructive (τ1/τ2 still correct) but leaves τ3–τ6 inert; A and E are
wrong. The published parameters are insufficient to pin the τ3–τ6 energies
to the level that makes them stable where Feng shows them.

## Conclusion and recommendation

This is the τ3–τ6 analogue of the suspected Table-3 row swap (WORKLOG §3):
the acceptance test surfaces that the published assessment is **not
reproducible for τ3–τ6 from the paper alone**. To complete them faithfully,
obtain the authors' actual TDB — the paper's Data Availability says "Data
will be made available on request" (corresponding authors huangkl0916,
qingry96, luzhao_gx). With their file, `tau36_block.py` can be corrected in
minutes (the site ratios and the GHSER convention are the only unknowns).

`tau36_block.py` ships hypothesis **B** (physically sensible, non-destructive)
so the phase definitions and the inferred site ratios are preserved for that
correction; it is **not** part of the production build and must not be used
for phase-stability work until validated.

## Impact on the WP4 work: none

τ3–τ6 are the Si-rich/La-rich ternary compounds. The magnetocaloric τ1
phase and its descriptor live in the Fe-rich corner, where τ1/τ2 + the
binary backbone are fully validated. The WP4 descriptor and the uncertainty
band are unaffected.


## Update 16 Nov 2026 — rerun with corrected Table 5 signs

An independent check of Table 5 against the PDF found three sign errors in the earlier
transcription (tau4 G(La:Fe:Fe) = +10001-5.002T; tau5 G(La:Fe:Si) = +48500-13.6T;
tau6 L = -65006.5+10T). They are corrected in table5_parameters.md and tau36_block.py.
Rerun (tau36_rerun.py, 21 alloys, 1373 K, hypotheses A/B/E, old vs corrected signs):
the conclusion does not change. A and B never make tau3-tau6 stable (identical to the run
without them; 5/21 exact phase-set matches vs experiment); E lets tau4 take over the
diagram (0/21). The missing piece is the reference/scaling (GHSER terms, site ratios),
not the signs. tau3-tau6 stay excluded from the WP4b descriptor.
Record: WP4b_Step3_Tau36_Rerun_20261116.md (private documentation repo).-e
